note: Literature confirms dark-adapted electronegative ERG is a key discriminator seen in early CLN3 presentations and absent in early-onset STGD1.

evidence.text: In children presenting with rapid vision loss, dark-adapted full-field ERG responses were either absent or electronegative in CLN3 disease, whereas DA ERG responses were generally unaffected and none had an electronegative ERG in early-onset STGD1.

source.title: Recognizing differentiating clinical signs of CLN3 disease (Batten disease) at presentation
source.quote: In CLN3 disease, dark-adapted (DA) full-field electroretinogram (ERG) responses were either absent or electronegative. In early-onset STGD1, DA ERG responses were generally unaffected. None of the STGD1 patients had an electronegative ERG.

evidence.text: In 5 confirmed CLN3 pediatric patients evaluated for early visual decline, electronegative ERGs were identified in all patients at presentation.

source.title: Early recognition of CLN3 disease facilitated by visual electrophysiology and multimodal imaging
source.quote: Electronegative ERGs were identified in all patients.
